title: Numbers, Get Em!
description:
You are given a string that may contain letters, digits and other symbols. Find the sum of all the digits that appear in the string.

For example, in Hello12345World!56789 the digits are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, whose sum is 50.

Input

A single line containing the string s.

Output

A single integer: the sum of all digits in s. If there are no digits, print 0.
solution:
s = input()
print(sum(int(ch) for ch in s if ch.isdigit()))

title: Is Subsequence
description:
Given two strings S and T, determine whether S is a subsequence of T.

A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more characters from T without changing the order of the remaining characters. For example, ace is a subsequence of abcde, but aec is not. The empty string is a subsequence of every string.

Input

  • Line 1: the string S (may be empty).
  • Line 2: the string T.

Output

Print True if S is a subsequence of T, otherwise print False.
solution:
s = input()
t = input()
i = 0
for ch in t:
    if i < len(s) and ch == s[i]:
        i += 1
print(i == len(s))

title: Quadratic Equation Solver
description:
Solve the quadratic equation a·x² + b·x + c = 0. Compute the discriminant D = b² − 4ac.

  • If D > 0, there are two real roots. Print Root 1: x1 on the first line and Root 2: x2 on the second, where x1 = (−b + √D) / (2a) and x2 = (−b − √D) / (2a).
  • If D = 0, print Root: x where x = −b / (2a).
  • If D < 0, print No real roots.

All roots are printed with exactly 2 decimal places.

Input

Three lines containing the real numbers a, b and c, one per line. It is guaranteed that a ≠ 0.

Output

The root(s) in the format described above, or No real roots.
solution:
import math
a = float(input())
b = float(input())
c = float(input())
d = b * b - 4 * a * c
if d > 0:
    r1 = (-b + math.sqrt(d)) / (2 * a)
    r2 = (-b - math.sqrt(d)) / (2 * a)
    print(f"Root 1: {r1 + 0.0:.2f}")
    print(f"Root 2: {r2 + 0.0:.2f}")
elif d == 0:
    r = -b / (2 * a)
    print(f"Root: {r + 0.0:.2f}")
else:
    print("No real roots")

title: Shortest Character Distance
description:
Given a string s and a character c that occurs in s, compute for every index i the distance from i to the closest occurrence of c in s. The distance between indices i and j is |i − j|.

For example, for s = loveleetcode and c = e the answer is [3, 2, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0].

Input

  • Line 1: the string s.
  • Line 2: a single character c (guaranteed to appear in s).

Output

The list of distances in Python list format, e.g. [1, 0, 1].
solution:
s = input()
c = input()
n = len(s)
res = [n] * n
prev = -n
for i in range(n):
    if s[i] == c:
        prev = i
    res[i] = i - prev
nxt = 2 * n
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    if s[i] == c:
        nxt = i
    res[i] = min(res[i], nxt - i)
print(res)

title: Balanced Parentheses
description:
Given a string consisting only of the characters (, ), [, ], { and }, determine whether it is balanced: every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, and brackets are closed in the correct order.

Input

A single line containing the bracket string.

Output

Print Valid if the string is balanced, otherwise print Invalid.

title: Balanced Array
description:
Given an array of N integers, determine whether it can be split at some index into a non-empty left part and a non-empty right part (both contiguous, together covering the whole array) such that the sum of the left part equals the sum of the right part.

For example, 1 2 3 6 can be split as [1, 2, 3] | [6] (both sums are 6), but no split of 1 2 3 3 gives equal sums.

Input

  • Line 1: an integer N (N ≥ 1).
  • Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output

Print The array can be split into two parts with equal sum. if such a split exists, otherwise print The array cannot be split into two parts with equal sum.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
total = sum(a)
left = 0
found = False
for i in range(n - 1):
    left += a[i]
    if left * 2 == total:
        found = True
        break
if found:
    print("The array can be split into two parts with equal sum.")
else:
    print("The array cannot be split into two parts with equal sum.")

title: Find the Lesser in the Most
description:
Given a list of integers, find the value that occurs most frequently. If several values are tied for the highest frequency, print the smallest of them.

Input

A single line of space-separated integers (at least one).

Output

A single integer: the smallest among the most frequent values.

title: Duplicate Characters
description:
Given a string, find every character that appears more than once. Comparison is case-sensitive (A and a are different) and spaces are ignored.

Print each duplicated character together with its count, in ascending ASCII order of the characters.

Input

A single line containing the string.

Output

For each duplicated character print a line c: count. If no character repeats, print No duplicates.

title: Valid Number Checker
description:
Determine whether a given string represents a valid decimal number. A valid number has:

  • an optional sign + or -,
  • followed by digits with an optional decimal point (12, 12., 12.5, .5) — at least one digit is required,
  • optionally followed by an exponent: e or E, an optional sign, and at least one digit (e.g. 1e10, 2.5E-3).

Nothing else is allowed (no inf, nan, letters, or internal spaces). Leading and trailing spaces on the line are ignored.

Input

A single line containing the string.

Output

Print Valid decimal number or Invalid decimal number.
solution:
import re
s = input().strip()
pattern = r'[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?'
if re.fullmatch(pattern, s):
    print("Valid decimal number")
else:
    print("Invalid decimal number")

title: 12-Hour to 24-Hour Time Converter
description:
Convert a time given in 12-hour format hh:mm AM or hh:mm PM to 24-hour format HH:MM.

Remember: 12:xx AM is 00:xx, and 12:xx PM is 12:xx.

Input

A single line in the form hh:mm AM or hh:mm PM (01 ≤ hh ≤ 12, 00 ≤ mm ≤ 59).

Output

The time in 24-hour format HH:MM, both parts with two digits.
solution:
t, period = input().split()
h, m = map(int, t.split(':'))
if period == "AM":
    h = 0 if h == 12 else h
else:
    h = 12 if h == 12 else h + 12
print(f"{h:02d}:{m:02d}")

title: Replace Elements with Greatest Element on Right Side
description:
Given an array of N integers, replace every element with the greatest element among the elements to its right, and replace the last element with -1.

For example, 17 18 5 4 6 1 becomes 18 6 6 6 1 -1.

Input

  • Line 1: an integer N (N ≥ 1).
  • Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output

The modified array, space-separated, on one line.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
res = [0] * n
mx = -1
first = True
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    res[i] = -1 if first else mx
    mx = a[i] if first else max(mx, a[i])
    first = False
print(*res)

title: Basic Calculator
description:
Write a simple calculator. Read two numbers and an operator, then print the result of applying the operator to the two numbers (first operand on the left).

Supported operators: +, -, *, /. If the operation is division and the second number is zero, print Error: Division by zero.

Input

  • Line 1: the first number (a real number).
  • Line 2: the second number (a real number).
  • Line 3: the operator, one of + - * /.

Output

The result with exactly 2 decimal places, or Error: Division by zero.

title: Hourglass Pattern
description:
Given an integer n, print an hourglass of stars with 2n + 1 rows.

The top row has 2n + 1 stars. Each following row has 2 fewer stars and is shifted right by one space, until the middle row, which has a single *. The bottom half mirrors the top half. Each row is centered using leading spaces only — there must be no trailing spaces.

For n = 2:

*****
 ***
  *
 ***
*****

Input

A single integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 20).

Output

The hourglass pattern, 2n + 1 lines.

title: Return to Origin
description:
A robot starts at position (0, 0) on a 2D grid. It receives a sequence of moves, each being R (right), L (left), U (up) or D (down), each moving it one unit. Determine whether the robot ends up back at the origin after all moves.

Input

A single line containing the moves string (only characters R, L, U, D).

Output

Print True if the robot returns to (0, 0), otherwise False.
solution:
s = input().strip()
x = s.count('R') - s.count('L')
y = s.count('U') - s.count('D')
print(x == 0 and y == 0)

title: Second Largest Distinct
description:
Given a list of integers, find the second largest distinct value — the largest value that is strictly smaller than the maximum.

Input

A single line of space-separated integers (at least one).

Output

The second largest distinct value, or None if it does not exist (e.g. all values are equal).
